body: I did, and that works as expected. I know that the error was on my side, not following the documentation exactly, but leaking client connections until they timeout is still something that should not happen I think. Perhaps there is room to improve stability even in case of application errors.

Hi @cescoffier @jponge 
I wonder, is is possible somehow to have a Quarkus code which catches the escaped exception outside of Uni, for example, outside of  https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/extensions/vertx-http/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/vertx/http/runtime/security/HttpSecurityRecorder.java#L96, and awakens the Uni which would otherwise be activated with `Uni.createFrom().failure(...)` ?

I will certainly document that one should avoid throwing the exceptions directly, but it is not the first time an issue like this one has been opened :-)
What do you think ? Also CC @stuartwdouglas

IMHO it would be nice if any `Uni`-returning API that is supposed to be implemented by application developers is at some point wrapped with a stupidity-protection-wrapper that logs and wraps unchecked exceptions and tells the developer to get some more coffee and take a break. It took me a while to find my error, because I first thought it was related to  #13478 somehow or the HTTP client I'm using was misbehaving or misconfigured.

@sberyozkin I don't understand.

In a Uni, if any stage throws an exception, that exception is propagated. However, in the code you mention, there are no unis, it's just a plain routing context handler.
